events.title: Publication of the Hangul Alphabet
events.description: According to traditional accounts, Korea's King Sejong the Great promulgated Hunminjeongeum, the document introducing the Korean alphabet Hangul, to the public. The script was designed to be easy to learn so that ordinary people could read and write.
events.significance: Hangul became the primary writing system of Korea, greatly increasing literacy. The date is commemorated as Hangul Day, a national holiday in South Korea.

events.title: Washington Monument Opens to the Public
events.description: The Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., was opened to the public after decades of construction delays. At the time of its completion it was the tallest structure in the world, at about 555 feet.
events.significance: The monument became a central symbol of national commemoration of George Washington and a defining feature of the National Mall.

events.title: Death of Che Guevara
events.description: Argentine-born revolutionary Ernesto 'Che' Guevara was executed in La Higuera, Bolivia, a day after being captured by Bolivian forces aided by CIA-trained personnel while leading a guerrilla campaign.
events.significance: His death ended his attempt to spread revolution in Latin America, and he became a lasting global icon of revolutionary struggle and counterculture.

events.title: Birth of John Lennon
events.description: John Lennon was born in Liverpool, England. He co-founded The Beatles and later pursued a solo career and peace activism.
events.significance: Lennon became one of the most influential musicians and songwriters of the 20th century, and songs like 'Imagine' made him a symbol of the peace movement.

events.title: Universal Postal Union Established
events.description: The General Postal Union was founded by the Treaty of Bern, with representatives from 22 nations, to coordinate international mail exchange. It was later renamed the Universal Postal Union.
events.significance: The treaty created a unified postal territory with standardized rules, making international mail simpler and more reliable. World Post Day is celebrated on October 9 in its honor.
